content_html:
A washer should not be packed tight with clothing. Items need room to move, wet out, and rinse; the real limit depends on the model's weight capacity and the type of load. As a practical rule, load clothes loosely and respect the manufacturer's capacity instead of compressing them to fit one more item.

Use the manufacturer's rated load capacity

Rated capacity refers to dry laundry weight and can vary by cycle. Comforters, rugs, and bulky items may fill the drum before reaching that weight and can have separate instructions.

Load items loosely rather than packing them

In a front loader, clothes need to tumble and move; in a top loader they should not be packed tightly around the agitator or impeller. Pushing items down reduces water and detergent circulation.

Absorbent items become much heavier when wet

Towels, blankets, and small rugs can look moderate when dry but become very heavy when wet. If the drum bangs, cannot spin, or repeatedly redistributes, reduce the load.

Overloading hurts cleaning and stresses components

Residue, dry patches, severe wrinkling, and imbalance are signs that there is not enough room. Two properly sized loads may use the washer more effectively than repeated rinses of one packed load.
